Traditional Vietnamese at its best
Jan 2020 • Friends
Fried spring rolls and hot pots are found in most Vietnamese restaurants in Saigon. However, Tuan & Tu has elevated it to a higher level. Before I go any further I must mention that the restaurant offers a varied and interesting menu. The starters of minced snail and pork wrapped in betel leaf, the special fried crab spring roll and fried minced squid and dill are by far the best that I've eaten beside the home made ones by my Viet friend's mum. The skin of the spring rolls were paper thin and crackling, and the packed filling was moist and additive to eat. The hotpot of river crab, pork rib and beef was exceptional. The soup base was flavoursome and less salty and murky then the usual southern version. Highly recommended if you are a fan of hotpot. Overall value for money.

They mess up and try to make you pay for it
Oct 2019 • Friends
The wait staff aren’t so great with English? So what happened was that whether or not orders were made wasn’t clear to them. On top of this the cashier messed up with order entry (accidentally only entering single orders where there were multiples of the same dish) so 20 minutes would elapse between orders being brought to the table. At the end of the meal, there was a dish that we did not order. We politely told the waiter that we would not pay for a dish that we have no recollection of ordering. He came back after to tell is that his manager insisted on us paying. We asked to speak to the manager. They made us wait 20 minutes and so we had to sit there while they decided on whether or not to bill us a 150k dong dish. 6 USD worth. On a total bill of well over two million dong without said dish. The manager never came by the way. We asked for the bill. They tried to sneak it on to the bill. We only found out when we asked our waiter to interpret the bill or us because of course it is in Vietnamese. At which point we also found out that we were charged 45k dong for rice when our waiter told us it was 10k dong. We insisted on seeing the manager again. The waiter informed us that he went home and that his manager would make him pay for it if we refused to pay. Again, all for around 6 usd on a 100 dollar bill. We had been sitting there for about 45 minutes at that point we informed them that we had no intention of paying for the one dish regardless. Attaching pictures to show just how much we had no problem with paying. I firmly do not recommend this dining experience. Pictures attached to show this is not a fake or manufactured interaction.

Worth a visit, even if it’s not as good as Cục Gạch or Quán Bụi
Jan 2019 • Business
Located in a cul-de-sac, this restaurant is pretty quiet. It specialises in northern Vietnamese cuisine. The food is good, but not as yummy as Quán Bụi (a few blocks away) or certainly Cục Gạch. They do have some homestyle dishes rarely found in restaurants, such as the deliciously comforting stuffed pigeon in broth. Tuấn tú means ‘handsome and bright’ in Vietnamese, but the décor is rather dark, a bit cold, and not very distinctive.

Northern Vietnamese foods as a style
Nov 2017 • Friends
I grew up in Hanoi, moved to another countries for many years, but the love of Vietnamese foods made by Hanion has never faded away. However, it’d been so difficult for me to find a restaurant where I can taste the real Northern Vietnamese foods, unless I was in Hanoi, until I came to Tuan Tu. Very tasty, very good. 
I would recommend the farm’s crab soup, spring rolls, pork stew in clay pot... 
Reservation prio visit is also recommended so that you can secure the table as the restaurant sometimes gets fully occupied.
